title: FY2026 NDAA UAP Briefing Deadline (Estimated)
description: The FY2026 NDAA requires AARO to deliver detailed briefings to Congress on NORTHCOM and NORAD UAP intercepts, including the number, location, and nature of each encounter. The legislation also mandates improved interagency data-sharing protocols. Exact briefing deadline TBD but expected in the first half of 2026.
expandedDescription: The fiscal year 2026 National Defense Authorization Act contains the most granular UAP-reporting mandate Congress has ever passed. AARO must provide detailed briefings to both the Senate and House defense committees covering every UAP intercept conducted by NORTHCOM and NORAD since 2004. Each briefing must include the number, geographic location, flight characteristics, and resolution status of the encounters, plus an assessment of whether any pose national security risks. The act also requires the DOD to establish formal interagency data-sharing agreements so that AARO can cross-reference sensor data from the FAA, NOAA, NRC, and DOE. Failure to comply could trigger subpoena authority under the committee's oversight powers.
keyPoints: AARO must brief Congress on every NORTHCOM/NORAD UAP intercept since 2004
Briefings must include number, location, flight characteristics, and resolution status
⏰ Estimated deadline: June 30, 2026 — exact date TBD
Mandates formal interagency data-sharing agreements across DOD, FAA, NOAA, NRC, and DOE
Non-compliance could trigger congressional subpoena authority

World's largest annual UAP conference, drawing thousands of attendees

title: NDAA-Mandated Deputy SecDef AARO Briefing Deadline
description: The FY2026 NDAA requires the Deputy Secretary of Defense to brief Congress on AARO's strategic vision across the Future Years Defense Plan by March 1, 2026.
expandedDescription: Separate from the broader AARO intercept briefing requirements, the FY2026 NDAA included a specific provision requiring the Deputy Secretary of Defense to brief the congressional defense committees on AARO's long-term strategic vision. This briefing must address how AARO's mission, resources, and capabilities will be sustained and expanded across the Future Years Defense Plan (FYDP), the Pentagon's five-year budgeting and planning framework. The provision reflects congressional concern that AARO — which only reached full operational capability in December 2024 — could face budget cuts or institutional resistance as political attention shifts.

Topics ranged from advanced sensor systems and radar analysis to satellite-based detection methods and machine learning approaches for processing anomalous data. The summit also addressed the policy frameworks needed to support systematic UAP monitoring, including proposals for civilian sensor networks and international data-sharing agreements. The event reflects the growing professionalization of UAP research, moving beyond anecdotal reports toward instrumented, reproducible observation.

title: James Fox UAP Press Conference at the National Press Club

The event drew major media attention and renewed calls for government transparency.

The event featured a panel of firsthand military and civilian witnesses, medical professionals who have examined individuals reporting close encounters, and current and former government officials with knowledge of classified UAP programs. title: DoD Inspector General Releases UAP Whistleblower Reprisal Report
description: The DoD IG published its heavily redacted final report on UAP whistleblower reprisal complaints, addressing allegations of security clearance revocation as retaliation.
expandedDescription: On January 7, 2026, the Department of Defense Inspector General released the long-awaited final report on UAP-related whistleblower reprisal investigations. The report, which had been in progress for over a year, examined allegations that defense and intelligence personnel faced retaliatory actions — including revocation of classified access and security clearances — after providing UAP-related information to members of Congress under authorized whistleblower channels. While the heavy redactions drew criticism from transparency advocates, the report's very existence confirmed that reprisal complaints had been filed, investigated, and substantiated to some degree. The release added momentum to H.R. 5060, the UAP Whistleblower Protection Act.

Confirmed UAP whistleblower reprisal complaints were filed and investigated

title: FY2026 NDAA Signed with UAP Provisions
description: The fiscal year 2026 National Defense Authorization Act was signed into law with three specific UAP mandates: requiring AARO to brief Congress on all UAP intercepts by NORTHCOM and NORAD since 2004, mandating interagency data-sharing for UAP investigations, and directing expanded Pentagon briefings on the number, location, and nature of encounters near sensitive military installations.
expandedDescription: The fiscal year 2026 National Defense Authorization Act was signed into law in December 2025 with three specific UAP mandates that represent the most detailed congressional requirements for UAP transparency since the creation of AARO itself. The law requires AARO to provide Congress with comprehensive briefings on all UAP intercepts by NORTHCOM and NORAD dating back to 2004, including precise data on the number, location, flight characteristics, and nature of each encounter. It mandates formal interagency data-sharing protocols so that UAP data from the FAA, NOAA, NRC, DOE, and other agencies flows into AARO's analysis pipeline. It also directs expanded Pentagon briefings to the full defense committees, not just select subcommittees, broadening the circle of congressional oversight. Disclosure advocates hailed the provisions but noted they fell short of the eminent domain and review board mechanisms proposed in the original Schumer-Rounds UAP Disclosure Act.

AARO must brief Congress on all NORTHCOM/NORAD UAP intercepts since 2004

The fully online, globally accessible format — titled 'Interdisciplinarity in Contemporary UAP Studies' — featured peer-reviewed presentations and panels exploring topics from exotic propulsion physics to the epistemology of anomalous claims. The conference represents the growing legitimacy of UAP as a subject of serious academic inquiry, with participating scholars from major universities worldwide.

title: 'The Age of Disclosure' Documentary Released on Prime Video
description: Dan Farah's documentary 'The Age of Disclosure' premiered on Amazon Prime Video after a limited Oscar-qualifying theatrical run in New York, Los Angeles, and Washington, DC. The film features former government officials, military insiders, and researchers claiming a multi-decade UAP cover-up. It broke Amazon Prime's record for highest-grossing documentary within 48 hours of release, with a 93% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes.
expandedDescription: Director Dan Farah's documentary 'The Age of Disclosure' debuted on Amazon Prime Video on November 21, 2025, following a limited Oscar-qualifying theatrical run in New York, Los Angeles, and Washington, DC. The film assembles an unprecedented roster of current and former government officials, military officers, intelligence community members, and researchers who allege a multi-decade government cover-up of UAP encounters and recovered non-human technology. Within 48 hours of its streaming release, it broke Amazon Prime's record for the highest-grossing documentary on the platform. Critics gave it mixed reviews (30% on Rotten Tomatoes), but audiences embraced it overwhelmingly (93% audience score). The film's cultural impact has been compared to the 2017 New York Times UAP revelations in terms of shifting public discourse. Steven Spielberg's upcoming 'Disclosure Day' (June 2026) is expected to further amplify mainstream engagement with the topic.

title: Sol Foundation 2025 Symposium — Lake Maggiore, Italy
description: The Sol Foundation held its 2025 symposium in northern Italy, convening leading UAP experts from academia, government, and civil society to discuss physics, governance, and policy implications.
expandedDescription: The Sol Foundation's 2025 symposium, held October 24-27 at Lake Maggiore in northern Italy, was one of the most significant UAP-focused academic gatherings of the year. Founded by Stanford professor Garry Nolan and former congressional policy advisor Peter Skafish, the Sol Foundation brings together a curated group of scientists, former government officials, and policy experts to examine the UAP phenomenon through rigorous academic frameworks. The 2025 symposium covered topics including exotic physics and propulsion, astrobiology implications, international governance frameworks for contact scenarios, and the societal impact of disclosure. The move to an international venue signaled the foundation's growing global reach and the increasingly multinational nature of UAP research.

The conference explored how traditional search for extraterrestrial intelligence methodologies and emerging UAP research could inform each other, covering topics from signal detection to observational evidence of anomalous phenomena. The event represented a significant shift in European academic engagement with UAP, with participating researchers from multiple European and North American universities. The hybrid format allowed both in-person and remote participation, expanding the reach of what has traditionally been a more insular academic conversation.

title: House Task Force Hearing: Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency
description: The House Oversight and Government Reform Committee's Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets held its first UAP-focused hearing. Air Force veterans testified about encounters with objects 'like flying buildings' near Vandenberg AFB. Rep. Burlison publicly showed MQ-9 drone footage of a Hellfire missile fired at a high-speed orb off Yemen that appeared to survive the strike. Witnesses called for stronger whistleblower protections.
expandedDescription: On September 9, 2025, the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee's Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets — chaired by Rep. Anna Paulina Luna (R-FL) — held its first UAP-focused hearing titled 'Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency and Whistleblower Protection.' Four witnesses testified: Air Force veterans Jeffrey Nuccetelli and Dylan Borland, Navy veteran Alexandro Wiggins, and investigative journalist George Knapp. Nuccetelli described massive objects he called 'like flying buildings' observed near Vandenberg Air Force Base between 2003 and 2005. Rep. Eric Burlison (R-MO) publicly showed, for the first time, MQ-9 drone footage of a Hellfire missile fired at a high-speed orb off the coast of Yemen in October 2024 — the UAP appeared to survive the strike and continued moving. Joe Spielberger of the Project On Government Oversight testified on the need for codified whistleblower protections. The hearing underscored persistent DOD resistance to sharing classified UAP materials with members outside the Armed Services and Intelligence committees.
keyPoints: First UAP hearing by the Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets, chaired by Rep. Luna
Air Force veterans testified about 'flying building'-sized objects near Vandenberg AFB (2003–2005)
Rep. Burlison publicly showed MQ-9 footage of a Hellfire missile fired at a UAP orb off Yemen
The UAP appeared to survive the missile strike and kept moving
Witnesses called for codified whistleblower protections (UAP Whistleblower Protection Act)
committee: House Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets

title: UAP Disclosure Advocates Push for Expanded NDAA Reforms
description: UAP disclosure advocates and bipartisan lawmakers pushed for expanded transparency provisions in the FY2026 NDAA, including broadened AARO authorities, mandatory reporting requirements for defense contractors, and a seven-year window for full disclosure. Congressional staffers briefed on the proposals called them the most ambitious UAP transparency measures attempted since the Schumer-Rounds UAP Disclosure Act.
expandedDescription: In late July 2025, a bipartisan coalition of lawmakers and UAP disclosure advocates lobbied for expanded transparency provisions in the FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act. The proposed amendments included broadening AARO's investigative authority to compel testimony from defense contractors, mandating that private-sector entities holding UAP-related materials report them to AARO within 180 days, and establishing a seven-year timeline for full public disclosure of all non-exempt UAP records. The proposals built on the framework of the Schumer-Rounds UAP Disclosure Act, which had been stripped from the FY2024 NDAA. Congressional staffers described the 2025 package as the most ambitious set of UAP transparency measures since that earlier effort. While not all provisions survived conference, the final FY2026 NDAA retained the core AARO briefing mandates and interagency data-sharing requirements.
keyPoints: Proposed broadening AARO authority to compel testimony from defense contractors
Mandatory 180-day reporting for private-sector entities holding UAP materials
Seven-year window proposed for full public disclosure of non-exempt UAP records
Built on the framework of the Schumer-Rounds UAP Disclosure Act (stripped from FY2024 NDAA)
Core briefing mandates and data-sharing requirements survived into final FY2026 NDAA

title: CBS 60 Minutes Investigation: Drone Swarms Over U.S. Military Bases
description: CBS News 60 Minutes aired a major investigation into drone swarms over sensitive national security sites, examining the 17-night incursion at Langley Air Force Base that forced the relocation of F-22 Raptors, as well as incidents at other military installations. The report highlighted the Pentagon's admission that it lacks sufficient technology to identify or counter the objects.
expandedDescription: On June 29, 2025, CBS News' 60 Minutes aired an in-depth investigation into the wave of unexplained drone incursions over U.S. military bases, anchored by the 17-night incursion at Langley Air Force Base in Virginia during December 2023. The report revealed that the swarms forced the Air Force to temporarily relocate F-22 Raptors — among the most advanced fighter jets in the U.S. arsenal — and that despite deploying multiple sensor systems, the Pentagon was unable to determine the origin, operator, or intent of the objects. The 60 Minutes team also documented incursions at other military installations and interviewed NORAD commander Gen. Gregory Guillot, who acknowledged the objects were 'small drones' but could not attribute them to any known domestic or foreign operator. The Pentagon admitted it lacks sufficient counter-drone technology to address the threat. The broadcast brought significant public attention to the overlap between drone incursions and the broader UAP issue.
keyPoints: 17-night drone incursion at Langley AFB forced relocation of F-22 Raptors (Dec 2023)
Pentagon unable to determine origin, operator, or intent of the objects
NORAD commander Gen. Guillot acknowledged the objects but could not attribute them
Pentagon admitted lacking sufficient counter-drone technology
Broadcast brought mainstream attention to the drone/UAP overlap

title: Scientific Coalition for UAP Studies Conference — Huntsville, Alabama
description: The SCU's annual conference featuring keynote by retired DIA official Jay Stratton, former director of the UAP Task Force.
expandedDescription: The Scientific Coalition for UAP Studies (SCU) held its 2025 conference in Huntsville, Alabama from June 6-8, themed 'Foundational Approaches for UAP Studies.' The conference featured a keynote presentation by Jay Stratton, a retired Defense Intelligence Agency official who served as the first director of the Pentagon's UAP Task Force (UAPTF). Stratton's participation marked one of the most senior former intelligence officials to speak at a civilian UAP research conference. Other sessions covered sensor data analysis, electromagnetic signature patterns, and proposals for standardized UAP reporting and classification frameworks. Huntsville's proximity to Redstone Arsenal and NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center added symbolic significance to the venue choice.
keyPoints: Held June 6-8, 2025 in Huntsville, Alabama
Theme: 'Foundational Approaches for UAP Studies'
Keynote by Jay Stratton, retired DIA official and first UAPTF director

title: AARO Announces New Options to Track and Manage UAP Reports
description: The Pentagon's All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office announced it is exploring new technical options to better track and manage confidential UAP reports, including automated feedback systems for witnesses and improved cross-referencing of sensor data. AARO's caseload continued to grow, approaching 1,800 active cases with over 1,000 additional reports retained in an archive for future analysis.
expandedDescription: In May 2025, AARO Director Jon Kosloski announced the office is developing new technical systems to improve how UAP reports are tracked, managed, and analyzed. Key improvements include an automated feedback loop for military and civilian witnesses who file UAP reports (previously described as 'informal'), improved cross-referencing of multi-sensor data from radar, infrared, electro-optical, and signals intelligence sources, and a more structured intake process for confidential reports. AARO's active caseload had grown to approximately 1,800, with over 1,000 additional reports retained in an archive for future analysis when better tools or data become available. Kosloski also indicated AARO would eventually open a public-facing portal for civilian UAP reports, though no timeline was given.
keyPoints: Automated feedback system being developed for UAP witnesses
Improved cross-referencing across radar, infrared, electro-optical, and SIGINT data
AARO caseload approaching 1,800 active cases, plus 1,000+ archived reports
Public-facing civilian reporting portal under consideration (no timeline given)
Structured intake process replacing the previous informal system

title: New UAP Legislation Drafted as Congress Prepares for More Hearings
description: House lawmakers announced new legislative proposals and plans for at least two additional hearings on UAP as part of an ongoing campaign to enhance government investigations. The UAP Whistleblower Protection Act, introduced by Reps. Tim Burchett and Anna Paulina Luna, would codify distinct protections for those disclosing information about government-funded UAP research programs.
expandedDescription: In early May 2025, a group of House lawmakers announced new legislative proposals targeting UAP transparency and whistleblower protection. The centerpiece was the UAP Whistleblower Protection Act, co-introduced by Reps. Tim Burchett (R-TN) and Anna Paulina Luna (R-FL), which would create statutory protections specifically for individuals who disclose information about government-funded UAP research programs, crash-retrieval efforts, or reverse-engineering activities. The bill would protect whistleblowers from retaliation including termination, demotion, reassignment, and revocation of security clearances. Separately, the newly formed House Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets announced plans for at least two UAP-focused hearings in the second half of 2025 — the first of which took place in September.
keyPoints: UAP Whistleblower Protection Act introduced by Reps. Burchett and Luna
Would protect disclosures about crash-retrieval and reverse-engineering programs
Protections include: anti-retaliation for termination, demotion, and clearance revocation
Task Force on Declassification of Federal Secrets announced two planned UAP hearings
First hearing took place September 9, 2025

title: National Archives Releases First UAP Records Collection
description: The National Archives released its first batch of records related to Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena, fulfilling requirements in the 2024 NDAA to establish a UAP Records Collection. Records came from the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, the Office of the Secretary of Defense, the FAA, and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. The collection is publicly searchable and downloadable in bulk through the National Archives Catalog.
expandedDescription: On April 24, 2025, the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) released its first batch of UAP-related records, establishing Record Group 615: the Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Collection. This fulfilled the requirement in the FY2024 NDAA that NARA create a centralized UAP records collection modeled on the JFK Records Act. The initial release included records transferred by the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI), the Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD), the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC). All records are publicly searchable through the National Archives Catalog and available for bulk download. NARA stated that additional agencies — including the FBI, CIA, and DOD sub-agencies — are expected to transfer materials on a rolling basis ahead of the September 30, 2025 statutory deadline, though compliance has been uneven.
keyPoints: First-ever centralized UAP Records Collection established as Record Group 615
Initial records from ODNI, OSD, FAA, and NRC — publicly searchable and bulk-downloadable
Fulfills FY2024 NDAA requirement modeled on the JFK Records Act
Additional agencies (FBI, CIA, DOD sub-agencies) expected to transfer materials on a rolling basis
⏰ Statutory transfer deadline: September 30, 2025 — compliance has been uneven

title: UAP Advocates Call for Transparency on Drone Incursions Near Military Sites
description: A coalition of UAP disclosure advocates including former defense officials raised formal concerns about unexplained drone and UAP threats to U.S. airspace, citing the unresolved Langley AFB incursions and the New Jersey drone wave. They called on Congress and the DOD to publicly acknowledge the scope of incursions near sensitive military installations and critical infrastructure.
expandedDescription: In late March 2025, a coalition of UAP disclosure advocates — including former Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Intelligence Christopher Mellon and former Rear Admiral Tim Gallaudet — raised formal public concerns about the growing number of unexplained drone and UAP incursions near sensitive U.S. military installations. They cited the still-unresolved 17-night drone swarm over Langley AFB (December 2023), the wave of sightings across New Jersey (December 2024), and additional incidents at other military bases that had not been publicly acknowledged. The coalition called on Congress to compel the DOD to publicly disclose the full scope and frequency of these incursions, arguing that the government's refusal to provide clear answers was undermining public trust and potentially compromising national security.
keyPoints: Coalition included Christopher Mellon (former DASD for Intelligence) and Rear Admiral Tim Gallaudet
Cited unresolved Langley AFB drone swarms (Dec 2023) and New Jersey wave (Dec 2024)
Additional unreported incidents at other military bases alleged
Called on Congress to compel DOD to disclose full scope of incursions
Argued government silence is undermining public trust and national security

title: Classified Congressional Briefing on New Jersey Drone Incursions
description: Pentagon officials held a classified briefing with the House Oversight Committee to discuss the unidentified objects flying over military installations and residential areas across New Jersey. The briefing followed weeks of nightly sightings of car-sized objects maneuvering over at least two defense installations. Federal assessments at the time could not attribute the drones to the U.S. military or foreign adversaries.
expandedDescription: In mid-December 2024, Pentagon officials conducted a classified briefing for the House Oversight Committee on Capitol Hill regarding the wave of unidentified objects observed flying over military installations, critical infrastructure, and residential neighborhoods across New Jersey. For weeks, residents had reported nightly sightings of large objects — some estimated to be the size of a small car — maneuvering silently over areas including the vicinity of President-elect Trump's Bedminster golf club and at least two defense installations. The FBI, FAA, and DOD all investigated, but initial federal assessments could not attribute the objects to the U.S. military, known commercial drones, or foreign adversaries. The classified briefing reportedly left members frustrated, with several publicly stating they received no satisfactory explanation.
keyPoints: Classified briefing held for House Oversight Committee on Capitol Hill
Weeks of nightly sightings of car-sized objects across New Jersey
Objects observed near Trump's Bedminster property and two defense installations
FBI, FAA, and DOD unable to attribute objects to any known source
Members of Congress publicly expressed frustration at lack of answers
committee: House Committee on Oversight and Accountability

title: AARO Reaches Full Operational Capability
description: The Pentagon's All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office formally reached full operational capability, meaning it is now fully staffed, funded, and equipped to execute its congressionally mandated mission. Lawmakers prepared for a classified UAP briefing as AARO transitioned from a startup phase to a permanent element of the DOD's intelligence infrastructure.
expandedDescription: In early December 2024, the Pentagon's All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) formally achieved full operational capability (FOC), marking its transition from a startup phase to a permanent, fully resourced element of the Department of Defense's intelligence infrastructure. FOC means the office is now fully staffed with analysts, scientists, and investigators; has secure facilities and technical equipment in place; and is funded at the level Congress authorized. AARO Director Jon Kosloski indicated the office would use its expanded capacity to accelerate case resolution, improve sensor calibration standards, and formalize relationships with allied nations' UAP investigation programs. Concurrently, lawmakers prepared for a classified briefing as the office moved into its operational phase.
keyPoints: AARO formally reached full operational capability (FOC) in December 2024
Fully staffed, funded, and equipped with secure facilities and technical equipment
Plans to accelerate case resolution and improve sensor calibration standards
Formalizing relationships with allied nations' UAP investigation programs
Transitioned from startup phase to permanent DOD intelligence element

title: Senate Hearing: AARO Director Kosloski Testifies on UAP Findings
description: AARO Director Jon Kosloski testified before the Senate Armed Services Subcommittee on Emerging Threats, presenting findings on notable UAP cases including the 'Go Fast' video (resolved as an optical illusion) and the Mt. Etna object. Kosloski stated AARO has found no verifiable evidence of extraterrestrial activity but acknowledged 'very anomalous objects' require careful study. AARO's caseload exceeded 1,600 reports.
expandedDescription: On November 19, 2024, AARO Director Jon Kosloski testified before the Senate Armed Services Subcommittee on Emerging Threats and Capabilities in both classified and open sessions. During the public hearing, Kosloski presented AARO's case resolution methodology and walked through findings on several high-profile UAP cases. The famous 'Go Fast' Navy video was resolved as an optical illusion caused by parallax — the object was not actually moving at extreme speed. A 2018 video of an object near the Mt. Etna volcanic plume was determined to be 170 meters from the plume, not flying through it. Kosloski stated that 'to date, AARO has not discovered any verifiable evidence of extraterrestrial beings, activity, or technology,' but acknowledged that some cases involve 'very anomalous objects' that require continued study. He reported AARO's caseload had exceeded 1,600, with the vast majority of resolved cases attributed to balloons and drones.
keyPoints: AARO Director Kosloski testified in both classified and open Senate sessions
'Go Fast' Navy video resolved as a parallax optical illusion — not extreme speed
Mt. Etna object determined to be 170m from plume, not transmedium
No verifiable evidence of extraterrestrial activity found to date
Acknowledged 'very anomalous objects' require careful study; caseload exceeded 1,600
committee: Senate Armed Services Committee — Subcommittee on Emerging Threats

title: House Oversight: Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena — Exposing the Truth
description: Second major House Oversight hearing on UAP. Featured testimony from military witnesses, government insiders, and UAP researchers on encounters, transparency failures, and alleged cover-ups. Members pressed witnesses on the existence of secret UAP programs and the adequacy of congressional oversight mechanisms. Former Rear Admiral Tim Gallaudet testified alongside other military witnesses.
expandedDescription: On November 13, 2024, the House Oversight Committee held its second major public hearing on UAP, titled 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Exposing the Truth.' The hearing was jointly convened by the Subcommittee on Cybersecurity, Information Technology, and Government Innovation (chaired by Rep. Nancy Mace) and the Subcommittee on National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs (chaired by Rep. Glenn Grothman). Witnesses included former Rear Admiral Tim Gallaudet, who described being told to stop asking questions about a UAP encounter during his military career, and other military and intelligence community witnesses who alleged a 'secretive arms race' involving recovered non-human technology. Members of Congress pressed witnesses on the existence of special access programs concealing UAP materials from congressional oversight and questioned whether DOD officials had committed perjury in previous testimony.
keyPoints: Second major House Oversight UAP hearing, jointly convened by Mace and Grothman
Former Rear Admiral Gallaudet testified about being told to stop asking about a UAP encounter
Witnesses alleged a 'secretive arms race' involving recovered non-human technology
Members questioned whether DOD officials committed perjury in previous testimony
Focus on special access programs potentially concealing UAP materials from Congress
committee: House Committee on Oversight and Accountability

title: Senate Armed Services Subcommittee UAP Hearing
description: Classified and unclassified sessions examining AARO's progress, case resolution methodology, and interagency coordination. Senators questioned officials on the pace of declassification, the adequacy of AARO's funding and staffing, and whether the office has been given sufficient authority to compel cooperation from other agencies.
expandedDescription: In June 2024, the Senate Armed Services Subcommittee on Emerging Threats and Capabilities held both classified and unclassified sessions examining AARO's progress roughly one year after the office began operations. Senators questioned DOD and intelligence officials on the pace of declassification efforts, whether AARO's budget and staffing levels were adequate for its expanding mandate, and whether the office had been given sufficient legal authority to compel cooperation from other agencies and defense contractors. Several senators expressed frustration that AARO appeared to lack the ability to access certain compartmented programs that may hold UAP-related materials. The hearing also examined AARO's case resolution methodology, with senators asking how the office distinguishes between prosaic explanations and genuinely anomalous encounters.
keyPoints: Both classified and unclassified sessions held
Senators questioned whether AARO has sufficient authority to compel cooperation
Frustration that AARO may lack access to certain compartmented programs
Examined AARO's budget, staffing, and case resolution methodology
Focus on distinguishing prosaic explanations from genuinely anomalous encounters

title: House Oversight: UAP — Implications on National Security (Grusch Hearing)
description: Landmark hearing watched by millions worldwide. Whistleblower David Grusch testified under oath that the U.S. government operates a multi-decade crash retrieval program and possesses non-human craft and biologics. Navy pilots Ryan Graves and Commander David Fravor described firsthand encounters with objects exhibiting flight characteristics beyond known technology. This hearing catalyzed the modern UAP disclosure movement.
expandedDescription: On July 26, 2023, the House Oversight Committee held what became the most-watched congressional hearing on UAP in history. Three witnesses testified under oath: David Grusch, a former intelligence official and UAP Task Force member turned whistleblower; Ryan Graves, a former Navy F/A-18 pilot and founder of Americans for Safe Aerospace; and Commander David Fravor, the Navy pilot who encountered the 'Tic Tac' object off the coast of San Diego in 2004. Grusch made explosive claims that the U.S. government has operated a multi-decade crash retrieval and reverse-engineering program, that non-human biologics have been recovered from crash sites, and that he and other whistleblowers have faced retaliation for their disclosures. Graves described regular encounters with UAP during training missions off the East Coast, calling them a flight safety hazard. Fravor recounted his 2004 Nimitz encounter in detail. The hearing catalyzed the modern UAP disclosure movement and directly led to the Schumer-Rounds UAP Disclosure Act.
keyPoints: David Grusch testified under oath about a multi-decade crash retrieval and reverse-engineering program
Claimed non-human biologics recovered from crash sites; alleged retaliation against whistleblowers
Navy pilot Ryan Graves described regular UAP encounters during East Coast training missions
Commander David Fravor recounted the 2004 Nimitz 'Tic Tac' encounter
Hearing directly led to the Schumer-Rounds UAP Disclosure Act (later stripped from FY2024 NDAA)
committee: House Committee on Oversight and Accountability

title: Senate UAP Hearing with AARO Director Sean Kirkpatrick
description: AARO Director Dr. Sean Kirkpatrick testified on the office's findings, case resolution processes, and the status of the historical review of UAP programs dating back to 1945. Senators pressed Kirkpatrick on claims of a government cover-up and the handling of whistleblower allegations. Kirkpatrick stated AARO had found no credible evidence of extraterrestrial technology.
expandedDescription: On April 19, 2023, AARO's founding director Dr. Sean Kirkpatrick testified before the Senate Armed Services Subcommittee on Emerging Threats and Capabilities. Kirkpatrick presented AARO's early findings and outlined the office's case resolution process, which involves a tiered analysis of sensor data, witness interviews, and cross-referencing with known objects and programs. He also discussed the status of AARO's congressionally mandated historical review of UAP programs dating back to 1945. Senators pressed Kirkpatrick on the growing claims of a government cover-up, particularly in light of David Grusch's forthcoming allegations (which had begun circulating in media). Kirkpatrick stated unequivocally that AARO had found no credible evidence of extraterrestrial technology or reverse-engineering programs, a position that would later be challenged by multiple witnesses in subsequent hearings.

Outlined tiered analysis: sensor data, witness interviews, cross-referencing known objects
Discussed historical review of UAP programs dating back to 1945
Stated AARO found no credible evidence of extraterrestrial technology
Position later challenged by multiple witnesses in subsequent congressional hearings

title: House Intelligence Subcommittee UAP Hearing — First in 50 Years
description: First public congressional hearing on UFOs in over 50 years, marking a watershed moment in government transparency. Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence Ronald Moultrie and Deputy Director of Naval Intelligence Scott Bray testified, showing declassified UAP footage and acknowledging that military encounters with unexplained objects are not isolated incidents.
expandedDescription: On May 17, 2022, the House Intelligence Subcommittee on Counterterrorism, Counterintelligence, and Counterproliferation held the first public congressional hearing on UFOs/UAP in over 50 years — the previous hearing was in 1970. Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security Ronald Moultrie and Deputy Director of Naval Intelligence Scott Bray testified, presenting declassified UAP footage and acknowledging that military encounters with unexplained aerial objects are not isolated incidents. Bray showed two previously unreleased videos, including one of a spherical object zipping past a Navy pilot's cockpit. He stated that UAP sightings are 'frequent and continuing' and that the DOD takes each report seriously. The hearing marked a watershed moment in which the U.S. government officially acknowledged UAP as a legitimate national security concern rather than dismissing the topic as fringe. It directly paved the way for AARO's establishment later that year.
keyPoints: First public congressional hearing on UFOs in over 50 years (previous was 1970)
Under Secretary Moultrie and Deputy Director Bray presented declassified UAP footage
Bray showed a spherical object zipping past a Navy pilot's cockpit
Stated UAP sightings are 'frequent and continuing'
Hearing paved the way for AARO's establishment later in 2022
committee: House Intelligence Committee — Subcommittee on Counterterrorism, Counterintelligence, and Counterproliferation
